user_locked: In Video 1, the rearmost child is replaced by the golden retriever from Image 1, using the dog's identity and appearance as depicted in Image 1.
In Video 1, the jacket worn by the leftmost child is replaced by the denim jacket from Image 2, and the original khaki-toned jacket is removed.
Video 1 is the edit base: framing, angle, camera movement, timing, 6-second duration, edit rhythm, scene, background and all regions outside the two edited areas are preserved.
The leftmost child's identity, face, hair and body appearance are preserved; only the jacket changes.
All children in Video 1 other than the rearmost child keep their identity and appearance.
reference_anchors: <Video 1>: one continuous 6-second medium shot; the camera tracks backward with the running group on a white daisy slope under warm low-angle golden light; the leftmost foreground child exits the left frame edge at about 2 seconds; the child at the left of the group stays in frame for the whole take and becomes the leftmost figure after that exit; the rearmost child stays at the right rear, fully visible, for the whole take.
<Video 1> provides the scene, lighting, framing, camera movement and timing that the two edits must fit inside.

<Picture 1> provides only the replacement dog's identity: golden to light-golden medium-length coat with longer fur on chest and legs, long droopy ears, dark nose, slightly open mouth with pink tongue out, sturdy medium-large build.
<Picture 2> provides only the replacement jacket's identity: blue washed denim, sherpa collar, metal buttons, "WILD CHILD" chest embroidery, patch graphics.
open_design: The dog inherits the replaced child's on-screen position, scale and running motion (running toward the lens on all fours at the group's pace), because the reference dog is a static seated pose while the source position is moving; this keeps the camera path and timing unchanged.
The denim jacket is completed as a worn garment: it sits on the running child with the fabric folding and swinging with each stride, instead of hanging flat as in Image 2.
Natural running sound details for the new group in the meadow (grass footfalls, the dog's panting) are completed from the visible scene.
No new event, cut, extra character, extra object or new ending is added: the video still ends mid-run as in Video 1.

content_events.text: The rearmost child in Video 1 is replaced by the golden retriever from Image 1, keeping that child's on-screen position, scale, visibility and running motion.
The rearmost child's own identity and clothing (brown jacket and khaki inner top) no longer appear in the video.
The leftmost child in Video 1 wears the denim jacket from Image 2 instead of the original khaki-toned outerwear.

developments.visible_change: Both edits are already in place when the video starts. On the daisy slope the group runs toward the backward-tracking camera: at the left of the group the leftmost child now wears the denim jacket from Image 2 in place of the original khaki-toned jacket, while that child's face, shoulder-length brown hair and body stay as in Video 1; at the right rear the rearmost child from Video 1 no longer appears and the golden retriever from Image 1 runs on all fours in that same position and scale, fully visible; the leftmost foreground child in the beige knit top runs close to the lens and exits the left edge of frame at about 2 seconds.
developments.outcome: Three figures remain in frame: the leftmost child now wearing the denim jacket, the center child in the off-white shirt, and the running retriever at the right rear, all still moving toward the camera.

developments.visible_change: The three remaining figures keep running toward the backward-tracking camera across the daisy slope; the leftmost child stays at the left in the denim jacket with the fabric moving with each stride, the center child keeps leading in the off-white shirt, and the retriever holds the rearmost right position, its coat and ears moving with the run.
developments.outcome: The video ends mid-run at 6 seconds on this three-figure formation, with the denim jacket and the retriever's rearmost position unchanged from the moment they were established and no new event added.

shots.content_purpose: Hold the source's single continuous take so both replacements are read clearly inside it: the leftmost child in the denim jacket and the retriever at the right rear run toward the backward-tracking camera, the leftmost foreground child exits at about two seconds as in Video 1, and the group keeps running to the end without any new event.
shots.description: The camera tracks backward at the same steady pace, height and medium framing as <Video 1>, holding the running group centered on the daisy slope. In the left foreground, <Subject 5> runs toward the lens smiling and exits the left edge of frame at about the two-second mark exactly as in <Video 1>, softening slightly in the near focus before leaving. Just to their right, <Subject 1> runs forward in the position they hold in <Video 1>; the original khaki-brown jacket is gone and the child now wears <Subject 3> - the washed denim sits open at the sherpa collar, the metal buttons catch the low sun, and the "WILD CHILD" embroidery and patch graphics are legible on the chest as the fabric folds and swings with each stride - while <Subject 1>'s face, shoulder-length brown hair and body remain as in the source. In the center, <Subject 4> leads the group in the off-white button-down shirt with long hair streaming sideways. At the right rear, at the same position and on-screen scale as the rearmost child in <Video 1>, that child and the brown jacket and khaki top they wore no longer appear; <Subject 2> runs there instead, on all fours and at the group's pace, the golden coat rippling in the backlight, the long droopy ears bouncing with each stride, the dark nose pointing at the lens and the mouth open with the pink tongue out, fully visible at the rear of the formation. From the two-second mark to the end, the three remaining figures - <Subject 1> now leftmost, <Subject 4> in the center and <Subject 2> at the right rear - continue running toward the tracking camera, hair, denim and fur moving with the same easy rhythm as <Video 1>, and the shot closes on this formation with no new action, cut or camera change. Synchronized sound: rapid footfalls through the grass and the dog's panting rise with the run.

uncertainties: The user calls the leftmost child's garment a khaki jacket, but the video evidence describes the left-of-group child's jacket as brown/rust and places the khaki-toned garment on the rearmost child's inner top. The edit was applied to the child at the left of the running group - the child who wears an outer jacket and becomes the leftmost figure after about two seconds - because the jacket type and position identifier match; if the user meant the leftmost foreground child in the beige ribbed knit top who exits at about two seconds, the second edit would target a different child.

The user did not say how the replacement dog should behave. The dog was given the replaced child's position, scale, full visibility and running motion so that Video 1's camera movement and timing stay unchanged, and the reference dog's seated pose, tennis ball and forest setting were excluded.

No audio analysis of Video 1 is available, so the soundscape was designed from the visible meadow scene and the running group rather than from observed audio; no audio reuse or audio reference asset was specified.
